A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOLD research, with matching authors, core architecture and experimental environments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-control experiments, comparisons with DreamerV3 and a non-object-centric baseline, and qualitative dynamics, attention and fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TD-MPC2 comparisons, additional non-object-centric baseline results and another fine-tuning case study.

M1.justification: Equation 8 revises the printed critic-training target, replacing the bootstrap coefficient 1−γ with 1−λ. The SAVi encoder-decoder, action-conditioned OCVP dynamics, Slot Aggregation Transformer and imagination-based training otherwise remain unchanged. This establishes a target-specification correction, not that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight relational manipulation tasks, Button-Press and Hammer from Meta-World, and Cartpole-Balance and Finger-Spin from DM-Control. PickAndPlace is renamed Pick, with the same task requirements and reward definitions. Additional comparator results and the new fine-tuning example use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds TD-MPC2 alongside DreamerV3 across all eight principal benchmark tasks. It also evaluates the non-object-centric baseline on Reach-Specific-Relative and Reach-Distinct-Groups, which v1 explicitly excluded. Table 1 and Figure 4 substantially broaden the central comparisons.

E3.justification: The added TD-MPC2 experiments introduce its default five-million-parameter single-task configuration, specified in Appendix E. Retained configurations, including 12-million-parameter SOLD and DreamerV3, the approximately 60-million-parameter non-object-centric baseline, pretraining budgets, rewards and success criteria, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The object-centric encoder ablation is extended to the two previously omitted advanced Reach tasks. Appendix G.3 also adds a Pick-Distinct frozen-versus-fine-tuned reconstruction case in Figure 15, showing the frozen model merging a blue block with robot components. The earlier fine-tuning example is retained as Figure 14.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds per method and environment. v2 Table 1 explicitly reports final success rates with standard deviations, whereas v1 Figure 4 presents success-rate bars without uncertainty. This improves uncertainty reporting without establishing additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds TD-MPC2 success rates and learning curves throughout the eight-task suite, including average success rates of 84.2% on Specific and 17.3% on Distinct tasks. Newly reported non-object-centric results are 39.2% for Reach-Specific-Relative and 5.1% for Reach-Distinct-Groups. Figure 15 adds a qualitative reconstruction failure. The retained Meta-World success rates of 100% and DM-Control returns of 497 and 645 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 8 corrects the λ-return recursion from γ((1−γ)R̂t+1 + λRλt+1) to γ((1−λ)R̂t+1 + λRλt+1). This is a non-equivalent mathematical correction. The remaining mathematical formulation and environment definitions are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion extend the performance claim from outperforming DreamerV3 to outperforming DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2. Interpretability becomes an explicit contribution bullet, although v1 already claims and demonstrates it. The central contributions concerning object-centric learning from pixels and adaptable representations remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 qualifies the sample-efficiency advantage by excluding Reach-Specific. Appendix A retains the deterministic-model limitation but removes v1's conjecture linking it specifically to weaker Cartpole performance. Appendix G.3 adds an explanation of the frozen model's failure through confusion between similarly colored block and robot components.

D1.justification: v2 documents the five-million-parameter TD-MPC2 configuration. It removes v1's reproducibility statement promising release of code, environments and pretrained models upon acceptance; this is removal of a commitment, not evidence that available resources were withdrawn. SOLD's implementation appendix, hardware specifications, hyperparameters and video link are largely retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix C substantially expands model-based RL positioning through Ha and Schmidhuber, TD-MPC/TD-MPC2, IRIS and diffusion world models, including an explicit comparison between IRIS's set-based representation and SOLD's object-centric interpretability. The main related-work discussion adds TD-MPC2 while trimming several object-centric citations, including GENESIS and SlotDiffusion.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, contribution list and results narrative, introduces explicit evaluation questions and a separate generalization subsection, and changes the title and Pick task terminology. It reorganizes the appendices, moves limitations there, and divides additional results into named subsections.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. The success-rate bar chart becomes Table 1, learning curves receive new comparator traces and colors, and the environment overview is split between Figures 1 and 6. Qualitative figures are resized or relocated, the existing fine-tuning comparison moves to the appendix, and a new comparison is added.

improvement.justification: The TD-MPC2 comparisons and completion of previously omitted controls strengthen the empirical assessment. Explicit standard deviations, the corrected λ-return equation and the additional fine-tuning failure case improve reporting and interpretability. These provide an incremental overall gain. Removing the promised code release modestly weakens reproducibility information, but does not outweigh the added comparative evidence and corrections.
